dek: Brent touched $114.00/bbl (oilprice.com, 5h) and settled Thursday at its highest since May 4 (Reuters: early Friday $112.96, -0.2%; WTI $98.12, -0.3%) after a 4% Thursday rally on Ansar Allah attacks against Saudi Arabia. sources: Reuters energy desk (oilprice), Reuters (Libya NOC head), Barron's, ING commodity strategy (via oilprice.com), Economic Times
fault_line: Fear premium vs real supply damage: is $114 oil pricing actual export loss (Libya shut, Saudi attacks) or just war speculation ahead of the Nov 3 midterms?

sections.what_happened: Brent touched $114.00/bbl (oilprice.com, 5h) and settled Thursday at its highest since May 4 (Reuters: early Friday $112.96, -0.2%; WTI $98.12, -0.3%) after a 4% Thursday rally on Ansar Allah attacks against Saudi Arabia. Libya's NOC head told Reuters on Thursday a pipeline valve from Hamada and Tahara oilfields to Zawiya port was shut, reducing production at both fields. France's 10-year OAT yields hit 5.071% — first close above 5% since 2002 (Barron's) — on fiscal concerns. ING revised its Q4 Brent outlook, saying the previously estimated $80/bbl average looks 'unattainable' as markets price a renewed US-Iran escalation.
sections.what_verified: Reuters oil desk, Economic Times, Business Standard, oilprice.com, Barron's all consistent on Brent/WTI levels; Libya valve shut confirmed by NOC head to Reuters; OAT 5.071% per Barron's.
sections.what_disputed: Barron's (22h): some analysts note oil is still a fear premium — physical flows through Hormuz remain 'remarkably resilient' (ING) with CENTCOM saying 95% of vessels passing; the rally may overstate actual export loss.
sections.why_matters: The war is now a tax on every household on earth: Brent at $114, a five-month high — while Libya quietly shuts a pipeline and France's borrowing costs cross a 2002 line. The pocketbook angle of the Saudi-Ansar Allah-Iran war.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE energy cascade — Brent hits $114 five-month high; Libya shuts Hamada/Tahara pipeline valve to Zawiya, production cut; France OAT yields cross 5% first time since 2002; ING says $80 Q4 Brent outlook 'unattainable'

totw_analysis: Our read: The war is now a tax on every household on earth: Brent at $114, a five-month high — while Libya quietly shuts a pipeline and France's borrowing costs cross a 2002 line. The pocketbook angle of the Saudi-Ansar Allah-Iran war. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Fear premium vs real supply damage: is $114 oil pricing actual export loss (Libya shut, Saudi attacks) or just war speculation ahead of the Nov 3 midterms?
